Plan travel in advance and follow diversion routes.

Heavy vehicles and long-distance travellers must adhere to prescribed diversions to avoid congestion.

Traffic Police & Highway Patrol teams will be deployed along the route to guide commuters.

🙏 Your cooperation is appreciated for safe and smooth traffic movement.

data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N

NVIDIA:

Nvidia sales set a fresh record but the company’s quarter-ahead revenue outlook failed to meet lofty investor expectations, sending its share price lower by up to 5% after hours. Note, the sales guidance excluded any H20 chip sales to China, which it said could boost revenue by at least a few billion Dollars; CFO noted it cannot pay the US 15% on China sales unless Trump's plan is formalized in law. Co. also announced an additional $60bln share buyback. CEO Jensen Huang said he sees Nvidia capturing up to 70% of the $3-4trillion in AI infra spend forecast over the next five years, saying this and next year are set to be record-breaking again for the company. (Newswires)

MACRO:

BoJ's Nakagawa reiterated that the BOJ will keep raising interest rates if the economy moves in line with its forecasts. In particular, Nakagawa underscored the importance of the results from the BOJ's upcoming "tankan" business sentiment survey on October 1st to gauge the impact of trade negotiations. (RTRS)

Japan's top trade negotiator cancelled a visit to the United States at the last minuteon Thursday, further delaying talks designed to finalise a $550 billion investment package offered by Tokyo in exchange for relief on punishing tariffs. (RTRS)

Foreign investors were net sellers of Japanese stocks in the week to August 20, for the first time in nine weeks, as they turned cautious, moving to lock in profits after a selloff in technology stocks stalled a market rally. (RTRS)

Citigroup Inc.’s strategists recommended adding to bets that longer-term US bonds will underperform and the dollar will decline due to the risk that President Donald Trump will undermine the Federal Reserve’s political independence. (BBG)

The Mexican government plans to increase tariffs on China as part of its 2026 budget proposal next month, protecting the nation’s businesses from cheap imports and satisfying a longstanding demand of US President Donald Trump. (BBG)

China’s commercial banks are tightening oversight of clients using credit cards to fund stock investments as small-time investors pour in to catch the nation’s $1 trillion market rally. (BBG)

The Chinese yuan’s limited offshore supply is posing operational challenges for United Overseas Bank Ltd., as more regional economies conduct trades and payments in the currency, according to an executive at the Singapore bank. (BBG)

China will push to cut steel production between 2025 and 2026, according to an official document reviewed by Reuters and a source with knowledge of the matter, as it tackles overcapacity that has hit prices and fed a worldwide protectionist backlash. (RTRS)

China is ready to manage differences with Canada through constructive methods and pragmatic actions, its top trade negotiator Li Chenggang expressed at an economic and trade meeting in Ottawa. (RTRS)

A tanker with a shipment of liquefied natural gas from a US-sanctioned export facility in Russia has docked at a Chinese terminal for the first time, the latest move by Moscow to expand fuel deliveries into Asia. (BBG)

Europe’s new-car market rose the most in 15 months in July, as consumers shrugged off concerns over the global economy to splash out on fully electric and hybrid models. (BBG)

UK Treasury is said to be considering a tax hike on landlords by imposing national insurance on rental income ahead of Chancellor Reeves’ autumn budget. (The Times via Newsquawk)

Canada’s state-owned Trans Mountain Corp. is gearing up for more growth on its recently expanded pipeline system by inviting oil shippers to sign up for more capacity. (BBG)

Alberta plans to impose a 2% levy on the computer hardware used in large data centers starting at the end of next year. The tax will apply to data centers with a load of 75 megawatts or larger and will go into effect Dec. 31, 2026. (BBG)

Australian business investment edged higher in the June quarter as strength in data centres and logistics helped offset a pullback in mining, while firms also revised up spending plans for the year ahead. (RTRS)

New Zealand's business confidence rose in August, with firms expecting better business conditions ahead as inflation indicators ease, an ANZ Bank survey showed on Thursday. (RTRS)

New Zealand wealth fund bets European stocks will beat US over coming decade. (FT)

The South Korean won strengthened after Bank of Korea Governor Rhee Chang-yong defended its foreign exchange interventions as efforts to stem the currency’s decline and said the won is part of talks with the US government. (BBG)

South Korea’s central bank held interest rates steady for a second straight meeting, reflecting caution over financial-stability risks even as it raised economic growth projections and kept policy accommodative. (WSJ)

The Philippines eased monetary policy for the third consecutive meeting this year, bringing the key interest rate to its lowest in nearly three years as inflation remained well below target. (BBG)

Argentine authorities said they successfully rolled over a large batch of local debt on Wednesday, passing a key test for Javier Milei’s strategy to contain a slide in the peso ahead of mid-term elections. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

The UK, France and Germany are preparing on Thursday to trigger a UN process to reimpose sanctions on Iran over its nuclear programme, European officials have said, in a move that would heighten tensions between the west and Tehran. (FT)

Taiwan’s top diplomat made a rare, unofficial visit to the Philippines on Thursday as the two sides quietly expand ties in the face of growing tensions with China. (BBG)

North Korean leader Kim Jong Un will visit China for the military parade on Sept. 3, a rare trip that would place him alongside other world leaders attending, including Russian President Vladimir Putin. (BBG)

The US, Japan and South Korea pledged to intensify efforts to block North Korea’s use of overseas IT workers to raise money for its weapons programs, warning that Pyongyang’s operatives are using increasingly sophisticated tactics to evade detection. (BBG)

NATO members are on track to spend more than $1.5 trillion on defense in 2025, according to the alliance’s latest estimates, as they build up their militaries amid geopolitical tensions and pressure from the US. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Samsung is reportedly considering a stake in Intel to boost chip packaging and challenge TSMC. (DigiTimes)

Alphabet Inc.’s Google is investing an additional $9 billion in Virginia through 2026 to enhance cloud and AI infrastructure across the state, marking the latest in a series of big tech investments in US data centers. (BBG)

CrowdStrike Holdings swung to a second-quarter loss and guided for lower third-quarter revenue than Wall Street anticipated, while lifting its full-year adjusted earnings outlook. (WSJ)

Snowflake Inc. shares jumped in extended trading after giving a strong outlook that overcame anxiety that software vendors will be hurt as the economy slows and new artificial intelligence companies take away business. (BBG)

HP’s third-quarter sales got a boost from growing demand for its artificial intelligence-enabled personal computers, a trend its chief executive expects to continue next year. (WSJ)

Trump on Wednesday fired Robert Primus, a board member of the railroad regulator that is weighing the proposed megamerger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. He was the only member of the board to oppose the merger of Canadian Pacific and Kansas City Southern. (WSJ)

Urban Outfitters logged higher sales and profit in the second quarter, but is forecasting a harder hit from tariffs than previously expected. (WSJ)

TSMC is expected to break ground on its first 1.4nm (A14) ahead of schedule in October due to a significant technology breakthrough, with an initial investment of NT$1.2 to NT$1.5 trillion (US$39 - $49 billion) according to supply chain sources. (UDN via @dnystedt)

BYD sold more cars in Europe than Tesla once again last month, according to ACEA data, a sign that Elon Musk’s electric-vehicle maker continues to face stiff competition from its Chinese rival as it expands aggressively in the continent. (WSJ)

Meituan shares plunge as China’s delivery price wars escalate. (FT)

Alibaba is in talks with banks to refinance a $6.5 billion loan maturing next year, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

Chery Automobile is planning a Hong Kong initial public offering that may raise about $1.5 billion as early as next month, according to Bloomberg sources, adding to what’s shaping up to be a busy September for new listings in the financial hub. (BBG)

Berkshire Hathaway, through its wholly-owned unit National Indemnity Company, has raised its stake in Japan's Mitsubishi Corp to 10.23% from 9.74% previously, Mitsubishi said on Thursday. (RTRS)

The parent company of 7-Eleven, Seven & i Holdings, is considering a $13 billion investment to support its overseas expansion. Seven & i Holdings is planning to spend approximately 2 trillion yen over the next several years as part of its international growth strategy. (Nikkei)

Toyota Motor's global sales rose in July for a seventh consecutive month, anchored by robust demand in North America and strong performance of hybrid and new electric models in China. (RTRS)

Pernod Ricard reported a 3% fall in full-year 2025 organic sales which met forecasts, but warned of lower first quarter revenues amid tariff uncertainty and sliding sales in the United States and China. (RTRS)

Hedge funds and private investors muscling into reinsurance threaten to destabilise the centuries-old market for catastrophe cover, a director at Munich Re, the world’s biggest reinsurer, has warned. (FT)

NatWest and Lloyds are among the big banks braced for losses on billions of pounds in loans to troubled UK broadband providers. (FT)

Swedish defense manufacturer Saab AB is developing its first dedicated missile to counter the increasing threat of aerial drones, with the aim of making the first deliveries next year. (BBG)

Lynas Rare Earths said it will raise roughly 750 million Australian dollars, equivalent to US$488 million, of equity to speed up its expansion, although cautioned a planned heavy rare earths processing facility in Texas may not go ahead. (WSJ)

DATA RECAP (Newsquawk):

Australian Capital Expenditure (Q2) 0.2% vs. Exp. 0.7% (Prev. -0.1%)
New Zealand ANZ Business Outlook (Aug) 49.7% (Prev. 47.8%)
New Zealand ANZ Own Activity (Aug) 38.7% (Prev. 40.6%)
Japanese Foreign Bond Investment w/e -167.2B (Prev. -313.6B, Rev. -310.9B)
Japanese Foreign Invest JP Stock w/e -496.8B (Prev. 1161.7B, Rev. 1167.0B)
Swiss GDP QQ (Q2) 0.1% vs. Exp. 0.1% (Prev. 0.5%, Rev. 0.4%)

LOOK: Progressive groups gather at the College of Science Library, denouncing the destruction of fishing structures and the ongoing reclamation projects in Manila Bay headed by San Miguel Corporation.

The groups called for the Supreme Court to overturn its decision last year which allowed the operation of commercial fishing vessels in the 15-kilometer municipal waters. Rommel Escarial, president of fisherfolk group PAMALAKAYA-Navotas, claims this intrusion has infringed upon the preferential right of fisherfolk, and the subsequent reclamation has caused flooding to residents in the area.

They also called for the courts to overturn a dismissed petition that sought to restore mussel farms in Navotas. Last year, hundreds of fishing farms in Navotas were dismantled under orders from the local government, depriving fisherfolk communities of their livelihoods.
